title: 03 The Four Fundamental Subspaces: Visual Guide
outline: Title: 03 The Four Fundamental Subspaces — six interactive visuals. The bridge from the elimination you already run to the four subspaces it hands you, then one panel per subspace and the counting law that ties them together.

1. Reading The RREF | THE BRIDGE. A 3x4 matrix whose every entry the learner can retype, with three rank presets; the live rref is shown with pivot and free columns labelled, a rank/nullity bar, and four boxes giving the dimension, home space and basis of the row space, null space, column space and left null space. | The one elimination you already do for rank answers every structural question at once: r, n-r, r, m-r, with row space and null space in R^n and column space and left null space in R^m.

2. Is It A Subspace | Five candidate sets (upper half-plane, the line y = x+1, the line y = 2x, the first quadrant, and {0}); sliders move v along the set and scale it by c, and three test rows report zero-vector, closure under addition and closure under scalar multiplication live, naming the exact c that escapes. | Closure is the whole definition: check the origin first because it is free, then try a NEGATIVE scalar — half-planes, quadrants and cones pass the origin and addition tests and die there.

3. Span Line Or Plane | Toggle u = (1,2,1), v = (2,4,c) and w = (0,1,3) in and out and slide v's third entry through c = 2; the SVG shows the span collapsing to a line and opening into a plane, while pills report vectors listed, dimension, the shape of the span, and whether the set is a basis — naming the redundant vector and the basis it reduces to. | Span counts independent DIRECTIONS, not vectors: one gives a line, two give a plane, both through the origin, and a set that spans is a basis only when it is also minimal.

4. Pivot Columns Win | A 4x3 matrix with a dial k that moves the pivot set; the ROW side checks every row of A against the nonzero rows of the RREF in both directions, the COLUMN side checks every column of A against the pivot columns of R and then against the pivot columns of A. | Row operations PRESERVE the row space and DESTROY the column space, so the row basis comes from the RREF and the column basis must be taken from A itself — and the rows live in R^3 while the columns live in R^4.

5. Free Variable Machine | Three reduced matrices (two free variables, a shifted pair, and full column rank); dials set each free variable while the pivot variables are solved and displayed, R times x is recomputed to prove it stays zero, and the special solutions are listed from the set-one-to-1-and-the-rest-to-0 pattern. | Free variables choose and pivot variables are forced; nullity is the number of free columns, the coefficient FLIPS SIGN crossing the equals sign, and the 1-and-0 pattern is what makes the special solutions independent.

6. Rows That Vanish | Weight sliders y1, y2, y3 mix the three rows of a 3x2 matrix hunting for the zero row, with a snap button for y = (1,1,-1); the same y is dotted with each column and with a choice of two right-hand sides b. | A left null vector is a recipe for a dependency among the ROWS, it is orthogonal to every column so the left null space is the orthogonal complement of Col A in R^m, and y-transpose-b nonzero is a one-line certificate that Ax = b has no solution.
